The Story of King Shrenik

I bow to Lord Jina, who sees and knows all things through the eyes of omniscience and is worshipped by the world, and I write the story of King Shrenik for the welfare of all.

Shrenik was the ruler of Magadh, with Rajgriha as his capital. Apart from several other subjects, he was a great scholar of statecraft. His chief queen, Chelna, was deeply virtuous, a devotee of Lord Jina, and adorned with right faith.

One day Shrenik said to her, "Look, Vaishnavism is greatly respected in the world and bestows happiness like no other religion. You too should embrace it." Hearing this, Queen Chelna, who had profound faith in the Jain dharma, replied gently, "My lord, very well. In due time I shall examine this matter."

Some days later, Chelna invited several Vaishnav ascetics to her palace and welcomed them with great honour. To display their piety, they sat down to perform worship of God with elaborate ritual. Chelna asked them, "What are you doing?" They replied, "Devi, we are leaving behind this body — filled with impure substances like urine and excrement — and attaining the state of Vishnu, where we enjoy the bliss of self-realization."

Hearing this, Chelna ordered a fire to be lit in the pavilion where all the ascetics were meditating. As the flames rose, they all fled like crows. Seeing this, Shrenik said to Chelna in great anger, "Today you have committed a great wrong against these holy men. Even if you had no devotion to them, does that mean you should kill them? Tell me, what offence did they commit that you thirsted for their lives?"

The queen replied, "My lord, I have done nothing wrong. What I did was in accordance with their own words, for their benefit. When I asked them what they were doing, they told me they were leaving the impure body and attaining the blissful state of Vishnu. I thought — if they attain Vishnu's state by leaving the body, then it would be even better if they could remain as Vishnu permanently. So I arranged the fire to help them shed their bodies quickly. If they truly believed what they preached, they should have welcomed the fire. But they fled — proving that their words were hollow and their claims mere pretence."

King Shrenik was struck by the queen's logic and felt ashamed. He realized that these so-called ascetics were hypocrites who spoke of renunciation but clung desperately to their bodies. From that day, his respect for the Jain dharma deepened, and he became a sincere follower of Lord Jina.

This story teaches that true faith is proven by conduct, not by words alone. Those who preach renunciation but practise attachment are exposed when tested. Queen Chelna's wisdom revealed the difference between genuine spirituality and mere theatrical piety.
